messages:
sam: Heads up — SIEM fired ~350 auth-fail alerts across multiple geo locations for a single staff account in the last 10m. Feels like alert-flapping/noise. Pasting condensed log: 
```
user: svc-datafetcher, src_ips: [203.0.113.12, 198.51.100.7, 45.33.22.1], result: FAILED_PASSWORD x347, device: api, svc: idp, region: eu-west-1 -> auth:fail -> rule: auth-geo-anomaly-v2
```
Can we triage before we start suppressing?

maya: I see the backlog. Looking at KMS access logs for that svc account — no corresponding kms:Decrypt or kms:GenerateDataKey calls in same window. That reduces impact risk. Also the account is a service principal used by a batch job that rotated creds yesterday. Could be a misconfigured runner retrying with old creds.

oliver: Good catch. We should scope by user_type. Right now the rule is firing on any failed auth. Proposal: modify rule to exclude service accounts that have recent successful auths from known CI IPs, and require >3 distinct sources + user-risk-score>50 for high-priority. Keeps noise down for bench jobs.

elaine: +1. We also need an interim suppression so incident channel isn't getting clogged. Suggest a 1-hour suppression for this signature scoped to user:svc-datafetcher and region:eu-*. That buys time to confirm.

sam: Agreed. Two actions: (1) create a short-term suppression; (2) update detection rule to add context checks. Who can push the suppression?

josh: I can push suppression via the SIEM console. Which query exactly? Want to avoid broad suppression that hides legit auth storms.

sam: Use this filter in the suppression rule: `signature:auth-geo-anomaly-v2 AND user:svc-datafetcher AND region:eu-*` — expiry 60m, note: "temporary suppress while we verify runner rotation". Keep suppressed_count metric so we can review.

sec-oncall-bot: suppression created by josh — id sup-8721, expires 1903460389, scope: signature=auth-geo-anomaly-v2, user=svc-datafetcher, region=eu-*. React with :eyes: to acknowledge.

maya: Meanwhile I'll open a quick eval query to correlate auth fails with CI job runs: `index=auth_logs user=svc-datafetcher | stats count by job_id, src_ip, outcome` — if job_id present => low priority. If no job_id and >5 distinct countries -> escalate.

oliver: For the longer-term rule change, propose the following heuristic:
- If user is service_account AND last_success_within_24h AND src_ip in corp_ci_cidrs => mark as benign
- Else require (distinct_src_ips >= 3 AND geo_distance_variance > threshold) AND (user_risk_score >= 60 OR target_is_admin)
This reduces false positives for rotated/duplicate job restarts.

elaine: Also update the dashboard: add a small panel that shows suppressed hits by suppression id, and a signal-to-noise metric (fp_rate estimate) per signature. That will make future decisions data-driven.

josh: I'll implement the suppression and add the dashboard widgets. Maya/Olly, can you pair on the rule change PR? Tag me so I can review suppression metrics after 1h.

maya: Yep, pairing now. Will open PR with tests and a sample of synthetic events to validate.

oliver: One more note — consider pulling KMS access patterns into the rule context. If a failed auth is followed by suspicious KMS usage or role assumption attempts, escalate automatically. Otherwise deprioritize. I can prototype the enrichment in the correlation engine.

sam: Perfect. Postmortem action items: 1) rule update (Olly+Maya) 2) dashboard suppression panel (Josh) 3) add KMS enrichment (Oliver) 4) runbook tweak to prefer user-type scoping for auth anomalies (Elaine). I'll file the follow-up ticket and link here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
